name: corduroy
notes: Combed clay, corduroy, drawn fibre: a tighter ring at 16 c/dia in a 12-degree wedge. Graphic and crisp where sand is loose; the narrower wedge is what straightens the crests. Rides the DEEP scattered train (dual scatter 0.7, spacing 0.07, n=12): a stationary Gaussian field averages to the same field, so it can spend the overlap that buys full scatter (docs/spectral-atlas.md §4). tonal.gain 3 restores the log-contrast that averaging costs; tonal.floor 0.02 stops one stamp's field minimum punching a full-ink speck through the stack. From the spectral sweep in docs/spectral-atlas.md; levels 30/55/80 are damage DEPTH, not coverage - moderate damage renders as moderate contrast over intact paint. Verified by tools/spectrum-audit.mjs. REVISED on review: crest axis turned 90 degrees (sectorAxisDeg 90), so the fibre runs ALONG the mark instead of hatching across it - a drag brush rather than a comb held sideways. sand already covers crests-across at a coarser scale, so the collection gets both orientations. Costs a little delivered contrast (10.6% -> 8.6%, since a narrow stroke shows less variation across itself) and cuts the train line from 2.6% to 0.9%.
